subsystems.name: Superinductance
subsystems.role: the defining element: a very large inductance with almost no capacitance, which makes the qubit's wavefunction heavy and localised in phase so charge noise barely moves it.
parts: chain of many series Josephson junctions, or a disordered high-kinetic-inductance film

subsystems.name: Josephson junction
subsystems.role: the nonlinear element that makes the circuit an artificial atom with unevenly spaced energy levels.
parts: aluminium oxide tunnel barrier between two superconductors

subsystems.name: Shunt capacitance
subsystems.role: sets the plasma frequency and tunes the ratio of charging to Josephson energy.

subsystems.name: Flux bias and drive lines
subsystems.role: fluxonium is operated at half a flux quantum, so a steady magnetic flux plus microwave pulses must be applied.

subsystems.name: Readout chain
subsystems.role: detects the qubit state without destroying it, at the low frequencies fluxonium uses.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic package
subsystems.role: keeps the circuit superconducting and shielded from thermal noise and stray magnetic fields.

buildSteps.title: Choose the circuit parameters
buildSteps.detail: Designers pick the Josephson energy, superinductance and capacitance so the qubit sits at a few hundred megahertz to a few gigahertz, away from unwanted resonances.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the superinductance
buildSteps.detail: Either a chain of roughly a hundred series Josephson junctions, each with a large critical current so no junction phase-slips, or a narrow strip of a disordered superconductor whose kinetic inductance reaches microhenries.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the Josephson junction
buildSteps.detail: Double-angle shadow evaporation deposits aluminium, is briefly oxidised to form the tunnel barrier, then deposits more aluminium — a process shared with transmon and RSFQ circuits.

buildSteps.title: Form the capacitors and wiring
buildSteps.detail: Capacitor pads, flux lines, drive lines and the readout resonator are patterned in the same lithographic stack, with reactive ion etching for the fine gaps.

buildSteps.title: Dice, clean and package
buildSteps.detail: Chips are cut, surface oxides and resist residue removed, then wire-bonded into a shielded sample box with well-filtered lines.

buildSteps.title: Cool down
buildSteps.detail: The package goes into a dilution refrigerator and settles at around 10 mK, well below the superconducting gap of aluminium.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate at half flux
buildSteps.detail: A steady flux is applied so the loop is frustrated at half a flux quantum, a point where the qubit is first-order insensitive to both charge and flux noise.

buildSteps.title: Benchmark and couple
buildSteps.detail: Coherence times are measured by Ramsey and echo sequences, then two-qubit gates are tuned up and their fidelities and leakage measured.

prerequisites.why: fluxonium uses the same junction technology as transmons and superconducting logic, so it can borrow mature foundry processes.
junction arrays and kinetic-inductance nanowires both work, but arrays bring spurious modes and losses and nanowires are hard to make uniformly.
the circuit only superconducts and stays quantum below about 1 K, so millikelvin cooling is mandatory.
coherence is limited by two-level defects at surfaces and interfaces; tantalum and other films have helped but are not fully solved.
arbitrary waveform generators, parametric amplifiers and dispersive readout are mature from transmon work.
randomised benchmarking, gate set tomography and surface-code decoders are needed to show the promised fidelity advantage.

pathway.milestone: single fluxonium qubits in research labs with millisecond-scale coherence and large anharmonicity
pathway.unlocks: a qubit whose levels are far apart, so drives leak less into unwanted states.

pathway.milestone: two-qubit gates at fidelities competitive with the best transmons, with measured leakage rates
pathway.unlocks: justifies using fluxonium as the building block rather than a curiosity.

pathway.milestone: multi-qubit processors where every fluxonium and coupler is fabricated within tolerance
pathway.unlocks: scaling to arrays big enough for error correction.

pathway.milestone: fluxonium-based logical qubits under surface-code or erasure-conversion schemes
pathway.unlocks: a lower-overhead route to fault-tolerant machines, if fabrication uniformity and readout can keep pace.
